summary.headline: PCBL Q4 FY26 carbon black volume rose 8% YoY to 161,865 MT while consolidated EBITDA was INR248 crores; management guides double-digit FY27 EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the West Asia conflict, which raised raw material, packing, freight and logistics costs and disrupted export routes. Consolidated revenue was INR2,066 crores and EBITDA INR248 crores, with carbon black domestic volume up 21% YoY and international volume down 10%. FY26 revenue fell to INR8,189 crores and EBITDA to INR1,081 crores from INR1,384 crores. Management says spreads have found a floor, pass-through and spot price hikes are under way, and net borrowings fell by INR454 crores to INR4,536 crores.

financial_highlights.change: -INR454 crores in FY26; INR750 crores capex funded

segments.name: Carbon black (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 161,865 MT (+8% YoY); tyres 88,591 tons, performance chemicals 53,888 tons, specialty 19,386 tons (+26% YoY). Management says EBITDA per ton was flat QoQ, so the QoQ EBITDA jump was mainly volume-driven.

segments.name: Aquapharm
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,443 crores and EBITDA INR162 crores; Q4 EBITDA INR29 crores on significantly lower capacity utilisation. FY26 volume 94,445 MT; home care +11%, water solutions -12%, oil and gas -19%, application-specific solutions +18%.

segments.name: Power generation
segments.commentary: Q4 generation rose 12% YoY to 196 MUs (175 MUs in Q4 FY25); external sales 116 MUs vs 100 MUs. FY26 generation up about 14% and sales volume up 17%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit EBITDA growth as volumes recover, cost and pricing improve; it expects FY27 carbon black EBITDA growth of more than double-digit.
Carbon black volume growth of high single digits expected in FY27 with the added 90,000 tons capacity.
Cost initiatives (yield, throughput, feedstock diversification) expected to unlock INR200-250 crores of savings over the next 4-6 quarters.
Full cost pass-through expected to reflect in numbers by Q2 FY27, when margin profile should normalise; Q1 FY27 profitability expected to improve.
Aquapharm top-line growth of 20-25% expected in FY27; management aims to return to INR50-55 crores quarterly EBITDA and the INR75 crores quarterly run rate over the next 2-3 quarters.
Working capital requirement of about INR100 crores incremental even if crude stays at $90/bbl; management still targets the 2030 EBITDA goal of INR40 billion.
risks_watch: Crude volatility (Brent near $120 at the call) and the lag in formula-based pass-through; the full cost impact flows through by Q2 FY27.
Logistics and freight costs remain elevated because of Cape of Good Hope rerouting; key US and EU export routes are affected.
Gas shortage delaying commissioning of the 1,000 MTPA Palej superconductive specialty line.
Competition from Chinese and Russian carbon black; industry overcapacity limits pricing power.
Working capital needs and net debt if feedstock costs stay high.
Aquapharm utilisation and the timing of green chelates approvals from P&G and Henkel.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term recovery and FY27 double-digit EBITDA growth, but openly acknowledges weak Q4 profitability and that the initiatives are not yet visible in numbers. Management is evasive on the coal tar project and the battery timeline, and gives no firm quantification on Aquapharm green chelates volumes.
key_quotes: As the environment normalizes and volumes recover, we are confident of delivering double-digit EBITDA growth fueled by volume momentum, leaner cost structure and better pricing realization.
Raj Gupta: So, from 2030 perspective, we are very confident ,we remain on track and with all the initiatives that we are taking, we believe that we should be able to deliver those numbers.
Q4 results are not what we aspire to be.
The platform we are entering FY27 with is materially stronger than we were 12 months ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in carbon black profitability this quarter, and how does management see FY27 volume and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said the QoQ jump is largely volume-driven (about 20,000 tons more) with EBITDA per ton unchanged, and the real impact of initiatives is not yet reflected. Nilesh Koul cited a contribution increase and inventory valuation lag; he expects high single-digit volume growth in FY27 and more than double-digit EBITDA growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per ton bridge for FY27, given ~14,900 per ton in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Koul said a 14-15% rise is achievable, driven by volume growth, product mix shift to value-added products, general price increases and cost initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pass-through and pricing work across tyre and non-tyre segments, and what is the Q1 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tyre contracts are Q-1 or M-1 linked while a significant volume is spot-priced with early price hikes; prices are expected to be strong in Q1 FY27 and profitability to improve, though some gains will reverse as crude eases.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and leverage: how will the company manage it while growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said borrowings fell about INR450 crores in FY26 and working capital investment fell; even at $90/bbl crude, about INR100 crores of incremental working capital is needed, and net leverage is expected to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2030 EBITDA target of INR40 billion still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Gupta said the long-term fundamentals remain intact, the headwinds are short-term, and the company is confident of delivering the INR40 billion target by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume and EBITDA uplift is expected in Aquapharm from P&G and Henkel green chelates allocations?
qa_highlights.answer: Pankaj Kedia said trial orders have started with supplies from Q2-Q3 FY27 and sales to rise significantly after approvals; capacity is 4,000 tons and will be expanded after approvals; the INR75 crores quarterly EBITDA run rate is targeted in the next 2-3 quarters, with no volume quantification given.

capex_capacity: Added 90,000 tons of carbon black capacity: Brownfield rubber carbon black expansion at Tamil Nadu completed in the quarter, taking total installed capacity to 880,000 tpa
Superconductive specialty black line of 1,000 MTPA at Palej, Gujarat is mechanically ready but commissioning delayed by gas shortage
20,000-ton specialty black line at Mudra is ready and expected to be commissioned in the next few weeks
Nanovace battery chemicals pilot plant at Palej fully equipped and ready for commissioning within weeks; a few months of validation before ramp-up; commercial volumes expected from FY28
FY26 capex of INR750 crores funded while net borrowings fell INR454 crores to INR4,536 crores
Aquapharm capacity expanded from 130,000 tons to 167,000 tons during FY26; green chelates capacity 4,000 tons, expansion to wait for P&G and Henkel product approvals
Coal tar distillation backward integration: feasibility studies underway; details and capex sign-off promised for next quarter
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 carbon black volume 161,865 MT (+8% YoY): domestic 105,055 tons (+21% YoY), international 56,800 tons (-10% YoY); tyres 88,591 tons, performance chemicals 53,888 tons, specialty 19,386 tons (+26% YoY)
Management says EBITDA per ton was flat QoQ; the QoQ EBITDA rise was mainly from the ~20,000-ton volume increase and inventory valuation lag
Spreads said to have found a floor; spot price hikes taken from March 2026, with formula-based tyre contracts (Q-1 or M-1) passing through with lag; full pass-through expected by Q2 FY27
Blended carbon black realisation guided at around INR1,400-1,500 per kg for Q1 FY27 (answer to analyst's question)
Customers stocking inventory: domestic customers held 3-7 days, now increasing cover by at least 3-4 days for both tyre and specialty customers
Around 40% of volumes exported; South Asia the main export market; US tariff cut and India-EU FTA (duty-free access to ~1.8 million tons market per management) cited as tailwinds

Aquapharm Q4: raw material prices up 25-30% (yellow phosphorus, acrylic acid, malic acid), packing material up to 1.5x; LPG disruption affected production; phosphoric acid price hikes taken from March
Power: Q4 generation 196 MUs (+12% YoY), external sales 116 MUs vs 100 MUs; bilateral pricing moving up and better realisation expected from Q1 FY27

growth.why: Management guides FY27 carbon black EBITDA growth of more than double-digit and high single-digit volume growth, backed by the 90,000 t Tamil Nadu addition, price hikes/pass-through by Q2 FY27 and INR200-250 crore cost savings over 4-6 quarters; Palej line is delayed by gas shortage and the industry remains in overcapacity.
